evidence_scope: Exact source-byte acquisition for Site01 near-field and first bounded-size large-area far-field raster inputs to LL-009L/M/K

source_pages.published_semantics: 5 m/pixel site GeoTIFFs; south polar stereographic X/Y meters; MOON_ME / DE421; total-Z product is RMS elevation uncertainty
source_pages.caveat: PGDA states that roughly 90% of the 5 m polar LDEM pixels are interpolated; nominal pixel spacing is not claimed as independent measurement support.

source_pages.published_semantics: 80-90 deg South large-area COGs; south polar stereographic X/Y meters; MOON_ME / DE421; elevation, surface-height-error and effective-resolution products
source_pages.caveat: Authenticating these rasters does not by itself prove that continuous terrain between raster support points is bounded by pixel-center skyline samples.

promotion_sets.claim_scope: Exact-byte completeness for the Site01 elevation + total-Z-RMS source pair only; not a complete terrain horizon.
Exact-byte completeness for the first Site01 5 m + 80 m large-area L/M/K trial source set; does not establish continuous-terrain skyline closure or site viability.

downstream_requirements: Offline replay of every locked source byte
Observed CRS WKT hash and exact raster-alignment checks
Separate closure or explicit margin for continuous-terrain / subpixel skyline support before any theorem-level complete-horizon claim
non_claims: No SHA-256 value is known merely because a NASA filename or source page is known.
The source plan is not a source lock and is not promotable evidence.
Nominal 5 m or 80 m pixel spacing is not treated as proof of independent terrain support at that spacing.
An exact-byte-complete source set is necessary but not sufficient for scientific horizon completeness.
